comparison.method: Exact app-owned Swift file bytes with matching basenames, including comments and inactive text. Each identical pair counts once in the distinct union. UI and logic are classified by whole-file primary responsibility, with native host composition that also renders UI counted as mixed.
observations: The two entry-save files are the same indexed source paths. The signed Android manifest also selects the same FieldLogDraftStorage.swift path compiled into the iOS app.

TaskEditorPresentation.swift matches byte-for-byte at its respective candidate paths. Source inspection finds direct callers in the iOS Apple fields host and no direct production reference in the selected Android Swift files outside the presentation file itself. Android PublicFactory builds its own MixerUI documents.

The iOS and Android WorkspaceRepository.swift variants diverge. The signed Commit host bindings are platform-specific. Apple uses SwiftUI and its native field host. Android uses a separate Swift UI factory and a Java/C bridge.

The stock Android installer selects NativeEntry.swift and PublicFactory.swift. The separate historical signed manifest also selects SignedChecklist.swift, SignedEntryCommit.swift, and FieldLogInstalledGuest. Stock membership cannot establish signed Commit packaging.
comparison.limitation: One observed compiler closure and two Android manifest projections. These counts cannot establish matched builds, installed behavior, direct Android UI use, or the 90% product threshold.
